claims.text: A CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational method can calculate melting temperature, entropy of fusion, enthalpy of fusion, and volume change at the melting point for novel refractory materials.
More efficient DFT potentials or algorithms can make these melting-property calculations computationally efficient while maintaining accuracy.
The initial material is a BCC solid solution.
CALPHAD can be incorporated into a high-throughput computational alloy-design method.
Refractory high-entropy alloys have extremely high melting points and are candidates for elevated-temperature applications.
Lattice distortion is a structural mediator in the proposed melting-property calculation.
Dislocation motion is a structural mediator in the proposed melting-property calculation.
The operative mechanism is thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
The intervention will increase melting temperature by 10–20% relative to traditional refractory materials.
The intervention will decrease entropy of fusion by 5–10% relative to traditional refractory materials.
The intervention will increase enthalpy of fusion by 15–25% relative to traditional refractory materials.
The intervention will decrease volume change at the melting point by 5–10% relative to traditional refractory materials.
The method is bounded to materials with melting temperatures above 1500 °C.
The accuracy of the CALPHAD-based method depends on the quality of the thermodynamic database.
The accuracy of the method depends on the efficiency of the DFT potentials or algorithms.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as a CALPHAD-based high-throughput method using improved DFT potentials or algorithms, whereas the mechanism is identified as thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamics; the hypothesis does not explain how these distinct approaches are combined.

A computational calculation method is presented as causing percentage increases or decreases in intrinsic melting properties, although such a method would ordinarily predict those properties rather than physically alter them.
